'''Oxtail soup''' is made with [[oxtail]], a cheap cut of beef.  In English usage the term "ox" reflects the social divide in England after the [[Norman Conquest]]: beef ({{lang|fr|boeuf}}) referred to the superior cuts served to the Anglo-Norman ruling class; the less favoured parts of the animal were referred to with the Saxon prefix "ox". The soup has been adopted in French cuisine, and there are examples from several other parts of the world. Being made with tough meat, oxtail soup requires slow, gentle and long cooking.
